newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil banks Icatu, Pactual may manage Bamerindus.
newsitem.headline: Brazil banks Icatu, Pactual may manage Bamerindus.

text.p: Brazilian investment banks Icatu and Pactual are the most likely candidates for handling the finances of troubled bank Banco Bamerindus, newspapers today reported.

Jornal do Brasil daily said a company to be called SPC-Special Paper Company would be created by the new manager, which would administer Bamerindus for two years and ready it for sale to private investors or to be given to the Central Bank.

The solution for Bamerindus then would be very similar to that of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj BEG.SAu which has been managed by private bank Bozano, Simonsen in a prior step to its privatization later this year, it added.
The new management, however, would depend on an approval by Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira, Bamerindus' majority shareholder, who apparently has already agreed to give up control of the bank.

O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper said Banco Icatu has already reached an agreement with the Central Bank to manage Bamerindus' finances. An official announcement was expected for Friday or Monday, it added.
A Central Bank spokesman said he could not confirm the reports.
Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth largest private bank, has been for months subject of speculation that the bank would be sold due to its liquidity troubles.
Earlier this year the bank announced a reorganisation of assets but market analysts expected more to come as the measure was not enough to help the bank overcome its widely-known liquidity problems.
